scope: Proposition 9.3 (One coupling for an interval) of the manuscript “Nonuniqueness of percolation on nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs” (preprints/Nonuniqueness-of-percolation-on-nonamenable-quasi-transitive-graphs-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 214 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 46a78d044d2713e4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 47. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let G be infinite, connected, locally finite, and quasi-transitive. Suppose pc < p1 < p2 < 1 and Tp2 is bounded on ℓ2(V ). In the coupling obtained by assigning independent uniform labels to edges and opening an edge at parameter p when its label is at most p, almost surely there are infinitely many infinite clusters simultaneously at every p ∈ [p1, p2].
